subject: mathematics
title: Perimeter of squares and rectangles
summary: Find the distance all the way round a shape.

lesson.text: The perimeter of a shape is the distance all the way round its edge. If you walk round a football field once, the distance you walk is its perimeter.

lesson.title: A rectangle 7 cm long and 4 cm wide
steps: A rectangle has 4 sides: two long and two short.

items: Square: all 4 sides are equal, so perimeter = 4 × side

lesson.title: A square tile with sides of 9 cm
Fencing a garden 12 m by 5 m

lesson.text: Always write the unit (cm or m) with your answer. Perimeter is a length, so it uses cm or m, not square units.

questions.prompt: What is the perimeter of a square with sides of 6 cm?
questions.explanation: A square has 4 equal sides: 4 × 6 = 24 cm. 36 is 6 × 6, which is the area, not the perimeter.

questions.prompt: A rectangle is 8 m long and 5 m wide. What is its perimeter?
questions.explanation: 2 × (8 + 5) = 2 × 13 = 26 m. 13 m adds only two of the four sides.

questions.prompt: Mr Adamu fences a garden 10 m long and 3 m wide. How many metres of fence does he need?
questions.explanation: Fence goes all the way round: 2 × (10 + 3) = 2 × 13 = 26 m.

questions.prompt: A square has a perimeter of 20 cm. How long is each side?
questions.explanation: 4 equal sides make 20 cm, so each side is 20 ÷ 4 = 5 cm.
